cards.explanation: The letter tells them to crown the best son and fight for Ahab's house. Jehu writes, "…select the best and most worthy son of your master, set him on his father’s throne, and fight for your master’s house." (2 Kings 10:3) I think that reads like a dare wrapped in a polite envelope.

The answer is False. They don't get ready to fight at all. The text says they were terrified, and then they send Jehu a message: "We are your servants, and we will do whatever you say." (2 Kings 10:5) They even add, "We will not make anyone king." Jehu's letter pointed out their chariots and horses, and their whole answer was yes.

The number is two. The text says they were terrified and reasoned, “If two kings could not stand against him, how can we?” (2 Kings 10:4) I think they mean Joram and Ahaziah, the two kings who had just fallen in Jehu's rise (2 Kings 9:24, 27). Their math was short and it was scary.

They promise they will not make anyone king. They tell Jehu, "We are your servants, and we will do whatever you say. We will not make anyone king." (2 Kings 10:5) Jehu's first letter had told them to crown the best son, and here they turn it down. They add, "Do whatever is good in your sight."

The answer is True. The text says that when the letter arrived, "…they took the sons of the king and slaughtered all seventy of them." (2 Kings 10:7) I think this is one of the heavy parts of the Bible, and it's okay to feel that. Then they put the heads in baskets and sent them to Jehu at Jezreel.

Jehu admits he conspired against his master and killed him. He tells the people, "It was I who conspired against my master and killed him." (2 Kings 10:9) The master he means is Joram, the king of Israel (2 Kings 9:24). He owns that part out loud, and then he turns around and asks who killed the others.

The answer is True. Jehu tells the people, "Know, then, that not a word the LORD has spoken against the house of Ahab will fail…" (2 Kings 10:10) Ahab was an earlier king of Israel (1 Kings 16:29). The part to catch is whose words Jehu says are standing: the LORD's.

The servant is Elijah. Jehu says the LORD "…has done what He promised through His servant Elijah." (2 Kings 10:10) Elijah was the prophet the LORD sent with a word for Ahab (1 Kings 21:17). The passage ends by pointing back to him too, with "…the word that the LORD had spoken to Elijah." (2 Kings 10:17)

The men say they are relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah. "We are relatives of Ahaziah…" they answer. (2 Kings 10:13) Ahaziah was the king of Judah, and Jehu had ordered him shot earlier in the story (2 Kings 9:27). I think they had no idea what kind of answer that was to give Jehu.

The word is greet. They say, "…we have come down to greet the sons of the king and of the queen mother." (2 Kings 10:13) That sounds like a friendly visit, like stopping by a neighbor's house with a plate of cookies. I think they had no idea what they were walking into.

The answer is True. Jehu asks, "Is your heart as true to mine as my heart is to yours?" and Jehonadab answers, "It is!" (2 Kings 10:15) Jehonadab was the son of Rechab, and he was coming to meet Jehu when Jehu found him. Then Jehu says, "give me your hand."

The answer is False. Nobody gets sent ahead. Jehonadab gives Jehu his hand, and Jehu helps him into his chariot. (2 Kings 10:15) Then Jehu says, "Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD!" (2 Kings 10:16) Jehu has him ride in the chariot, so he's going along, not out in front.

Jehu invites him to see his ZEAL for the LORD, friends! He's helping Jehonadab into the chariot when he says, "Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD!" (2 Kings 10:16) I think that's a big thing to promise a man while you're still pulling him aboard.
